questions.q: In this lab's scenario, what should block a user from setting Incident Priority to Critical inline?
options: Not holding the incident_manager role, checked with g_user.hasRole('incident_manager')
Being assigned to the incident
Editing the record outside business hours
The record being in a closed state
questions.explain: The scenario's rule is role-based: only users holding incident_manager may set Priority to Critical, checked via g_user.hasRole().

options: ServiceNow priority values are never numeric
newValue always arrives as a string, so the comparison target should be a string too
callback() requires string comparisons specifically
It's a typo with no real effect either way
questions.explain: Both onChange and onCellEdit pass values as strings, which is why '1' (not the number 1) is the safe comparison.

questions.q: What does callback(false) actually do inside the onCellEdit script?
options: Deletes the Incident record
Forces the edit through regardless of the role check
Blocks the pending inline edit and reverts the cell to its previous value
Switches the user into the form view automatically
questions.explain: callback(false) tells the platform to deny the pending list-view edit, reverting the cell — the onCellEdit equivalent of blocking a submit.

questions.q: In the form-level onChange version of this guard, why does the script call g_form.setValue('priority', oldValue) instead of something like callback(false)?
options: g_form.setValue is required before every onChange function can run
callback(false) works identically in onChange, it's just more verbose
oldValue is not available inside onChange, so this line does nothing
onChange has no callback mechanism — reverting the field requires explicitly setting it back to the prior value
questions.explain: Only onCellEdit resolves through an asynchronous callback. onChange has no equivalent, so reverting the field means setting it back manually.

questions.q: Why does this lab build two separate client scripts — one onCellEdit, one onChange — instead of one script covering both?
options: ServiceNow doesn't allow more than one client script per table
A client script attached to the list doesn't run on the form, and vice versa, since they're separate records scoped to separate contexts
onCellEdit scripts automatically apply to forms too, so this is just a stylistic choice
Only one of the two scripts is actually necessary; the lab builds both for practice only
questions.explain: sys_script_client records are scoped to their type and context — enforcing one rule on two UI surfaces genuinely requires two scripts kept in sync.
